19815-roy-blakeley-pathfinder.creator: Percy Keese Fitzhugh
19815-roy-blakeley-pathfinder.description: A book by Percy Keese Fitzhugh. This story is all about a hike. It starts on Bridge Street and ends on Bridge Street. Maybe you’ll think it’s just a street story. But that’s where you’ll get left. It starts at the soda fountain in Warner’s Drug Store on Bridge Street in Catskill, New York, and it ends at the soda fountain in Bennett’s Candy Store on Bridge Street in Bridgeboro, New Jersey.

arxiv-2101-07806.title: Non-Halo Structures and their Effects on Gravitational Lensing 2020 Non-Halo Structures and their Effects on Gravitational Lensing – 10
arxiv-2101-07806.creator: T. R. G. Richardson, J. Stücker, R. E. Angulo, O. Hahn
arxiv-2101-07806.description: Abstract Anomalies in the flux-ratios of the images of quadruply-lensed quasars have been used to constrain the nature of dark matter. Assuming these lensing perturbations are caused by dark matter haloes, it is currently possible to constrain the mass of a hypothetical Warm Dark Matter (WDM) particle to be m χ > 5.2 m_{\chi}>5.2 keV.

arxiv-2104-11646.title: The generalized 3-connectivity of the folded hypercube
arxiv-2104-11646.creator: F
arxiv-2104-11646.description: Abstract Abstract The generalized k -connectivity of a graph G , denoted by \kappa_{k}(G) , is a generalization of the traditional connectivity. It is well known that the generalized k -connectivity is an important indicator for measuring the fault tolerance and reliability of interconnection networks.

arxiv-2311-03308.title: Revisiting α ′ \alpha^{\prime} corrections to heterotic two-charge black holes
arxiv-2311-03308.creator: Stefano Massai, Alejandro Ruipérez, Matteo Zatti
arxiv-2311-03308.description: Abstract We find solutions of the heterotic string effective action describing the first-order α ′ \alpha^{\prime} corrections to two-charge black holes at finite temperature. Making explicit use of these solutions, we compute the corrections to the thermodynamic quantities: temperature, chemical potentials, mass, charges and entropy.

arxiv-2401-05922.title: Two-body 𝑷 \bm{P} -state energies at 𝜶 𝟔 \bm{\alpha^{6}} order
arxiv-2401-05922.creator: Vojtěch Patkóš, Vladimir A. Yerokhin, Krzysztof Pachucki
arxiv-2401-05922.description: Abstract We present an analytical calculation of the complete α 6 \alpha^{6} correction to energies of n ​ P nP -levels of two-body systems consisting of the spin- 0 0 or 1 / 2 1/2 extended-size particles with arbitrary masses and magnetic moments.

arxiv-2401-08716.title: Nambu and Compositeness Preprint: FERMILAB-CONF-24-0010-T Invited talk, Miami 2003,Topical Conference on Elementary Particles, Astrophysics and Cosmology, organizer: Thom Curtright, University of Miami.
arxiv-2401-08716.creator: Christopher T. Hill
arxiv-2401-08716.description: Abstract The Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model (NJL) NJL is the simplest field theory of a composite scalar boson, consisting of a pair of chiral fermions. A bound state emerges from an assumed point-like 4-fermion interaction and is described by local effective field, Φ ⁡ ( x ) \Phi(x) .

arxiv-2412-01535.title: Nucleon charges and σ \sigma -terms in lattice QCD
arxiv-2412-01535.creator: C. Alexandrou, S. Bacchio, J. Finkenrath, C. Iona, G. Koutsou, Y. Li, G. Spanoudes
arxiv-2412-01535.description: Abstract We determine the nucleon axial, scalar and tensor charges and the nucleon σ \sigma -terms using twisted mass fermions. We employ three ensembles with approximately equal physical volume of about 5.5 fm, three values of the lattice spacing, approximately 0.06 fm, 0.07 fm and 0.

arxiv-2504-00697.title: Auditory Localization and Assessment of Consequential Robot Sounds: A Multi-Method Study in Virtual Reality
arxiv-2504-00697.creator: Marlene Wessels, Jorge de Heuvel, Leon Müller, Anna Luisa Maier, Maren Bennewitz, Johannes Kraus
arxiv-2504-00697.description: Abstract Mobile robots increasingly operate alongside humans but are often out of sight, so that humans need to rely on the sounds of the robots to recognize their presence. For successful human-robot interaction (HRI), it is therefore crucial to understand how humans perceive robots by their consequential sounds, i.e., operating noise.

arxiv-2507-15357.title: Metaphor and Large Language Models: When Surface Features Matter More than Deep Understanding
arxiv-2507-15357.creator: Elisa Sanchez-Bayona, Rodrigo Agerri
arxiv-2507-15357.description: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) in metaphor interpretation across multiple datasets, tasks, and prompt configurations. Although metaphor processing has gained significant attention in Natural Language Processing (NLP), previous research has been limited to single-dataset evaluations and specific task settings, often using artificially constructed data through lexical replacement.

arxiv-2509-22645.title: Hierarchical Representation Matching for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning
arxiv-2509-22645.creator: Zhen-Hao Wen, Yan Wang, Ji Feng, Han-Jia Ye, De-Chuan Zhan & Da-Wei Zhou
arxiv-2509-22645.description: Abstract Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to endow models with the ability to continuously adapt to evolving data streams. Recent advances in pre-trained vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) provide a powerful foundation for this task. However, existing approaches often rely on simplistic templates, such as “a photo of a [CLASS]”, which overlook the hierarchical nature of visual concepts.

arxiv-2601-15613.title: A kinetic–moment framework for electron energy dynamics in capacitively coupled plasmas: absorption, conversion, transport, and dissipation
arxiv-2601-15613.creator: Jianxiong Yao, Zeduan Zhang, Feng He, Jinsong Miao, Jiting Ouyang, Bocong Zheng
arxiv-2601-15613.description: Abstract Understanding electron energy dynamics in low-temperature plasmas such as capacitively coupled plasmas (CCPs), including energy absorption, conversion, transport, and dissipation, is essential for interpreting discharge physics and process applications. We propose a kinetic–moment framework based on particle-in-cell/Monte Carlo collision (PIC/MCC) simulations.

pmc-10575181.title: Transcriptome Analysis Reveals Candidate Genes Involved in Gibberellin-Induced Fruit Development in Rosa roxburghii
pmc-10575181.creator: Xiaolong Huang, Xiaoai Wu, Guilian Sun, Yu Jiang, Huiqing Yan, Mikihisa Umehara
pmc-10575181.description: Gibberellins (GAs) play indispensable roles in the fruit development of horticultural plants. Unfortunately, the molecular basis behind GAs regulating fruit development in R. roxburghii remains obscure. Here, GA3 spraying to R. roxburghii ‘Guinong 5’ at full-bloom promoted fruit size and weight, prickle development, seed abortion, ascorbic acid accumulation, and reduction in total soluble sugar.

pmc-11409607.title: Accelerometer-derived moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and incident nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
pmc-11409607.creator: Mengyi Liu, Ziliang Ye, Yuanyuan Zhang, Panpan He, Chun Zhou, Sisi Yang, Yanjun Zhang, Xiaoqin Gan, Xianhui Qin
pmc-11409607.description: BackgroundThe liver effects of concentrated vs. more evenly distributed moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) patterns remain unclear. We aimed to examine the association of accelerometer-measured MVPA and different MVPA patterns with liver outcomes.MethodsEighty-eight thousand six hundred fifty-six participants without prior liver diseases from UK Biobank were included. MVPA was measured by a wrist-worn accelerometer.

pmc-11433310.title: Growth Characteristics of a Desmodesmus Species from the San Antonio Springs and Its Short-Term Impact on Soil Microbial Dynamics
pmc-11433310.creator: Lauren K Bomer, Betsy D Leverett, Milan Kolar, Pabulo H Rampelotto
pmc-11433310.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A new Desmodesmus species was isolated from the largest of the San Antonio Springs, the Blue Hole, in San Antonio, Texas, and characterized for its potential applications in sustainable agriculture. The xenic isolate (XB) was established by enrichment and subcultured to produce the axenic isolate (AxB), which was identified based on morphological features and DNA profiling, confirming its close phylogenetic relationship with Desmodesmus spp.

pmc-12567614.title: Hybrid Diagnostic Framework for Interpretable Bearing Fault Classification Using CNN and Dual-Stage Feature Selection
pmc-12567614.creator: Mohamed Elhachemi Saouli, Mostefa Mohamed Touba, Adel Boudiaf, Jiawei Xiang
pmc-12567614.description: Timely and accurate fault diagnosis in rotary machinery is essential for ensuring system reliability and minimizing unplanned downtime. While deep learning approaches, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have demonstrated strong performance in vibration-based fault classification, their limited interpretability poses challenges for adoption in safety-critical environments.
